name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q01 - Household food products and their associated microbes

questiontext.text:
Match the household food products with the micro-organisms involved in their production and choose the correct combination.

List I (Product)List II (Micro-organism)
A. Curd(i) Propionibacterium sharmanii
B. Bread(ii) Specific fungi
C. Swiss cheese(iii) Lactobacillus
D. Roquefort cheese(iv) Saccharomyces cerevisiae

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific micro-organisms are used in household food preparation to ferment milk, dough, and cheese, imparting characteristic textures and flavours.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Curd is produced from milk by lactic acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus, which coagulate and partially digest milk proteins.
2. Bread dough is fermented using baker's yeast, scientifically known as Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
3. Swiss cheese develops its characteristic large holes due to the production of a large amount of \(\text{CO}_2\) by the bacterium Propionibacterium sharmanii.
4. Roquefort cheese is ripened by growing specific fungi on it, which gives it a particular flavour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), and D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q02 - Organic acids and their microbial producers

questiontext.text:
Match the following organic acids with their commercial microbial producers and select the correct option.

List I (Organic Acid)List II (Microbial Producer)
A. Citric acid(i) Clostridium butylicum
B. Acetic acid(ii) Aspergillus niger
C. Butyric acid(iii) Lactobacillus
D. Lactic acid(iv) Acetobacter aceti

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Various fungi and bacteria are employed commercially to synthesise organic acids on an industrial scale.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Citric acid is produced commercially by the fungus Aspergillus niger.
2. Acetic acid is produced by the bacterium Acetobacter aceti.
3. Butyric acid is produced by the bacterium Clostridium butylicum.
4. Lactic acid is produced by the bacterium Lactobacillus.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), and D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q03 - Microbial enzymes and bioactive molecules with applications

questiontext.text:
Match the microbial enzymes and bioactive molecules with their respective commercial or medical applications.

List I (Enzyme / Molecule)List II (Application)
A. Lipase(i) Clarification of bottled fruit juices
B. Pectinase and protease(ii) Immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients
C. Streptokinase(iii) Removal of oily stains in detergent formulations
D. Cyclosporin A(iv) Clot buster in myocardial infarction patients

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbially derived enzymes and bioactive molecules are tailored to specific industrial and clinical functions based on their biochemical targets.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Lipase breaks down lipids and is used in detergent formulations to remove oily stains from laundry.
2. Pectinase and protease are used to clarify bottled fruit juices, making them clearer than homemade juices.
3. Streptokinase, produced by Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering, acts as a clot buster to remove blood clots in patients who have undergone myocardial infarction.
4. Cyclosporin A is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), and D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q04 - Bioactive products and their source micro-organisms

questiontext.text:
Match each medical bioactive product with its corresponding source micro-organism.

List I (Bioactive Product)List II (Source Micro-organism)
A. Statins(i) Streptococcus
B. Cyclosporin A(ii) Monascus purpureus
C. Penicillin(iii) Trichoderma polysporum
D. Streptokinase(iv) Penicillium notatum

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different bacteria, yeasts, and filamentous fungi synthesise distinct medicinal compounds used to treat cardiovascular, immunological, and infectious conditions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Statins, used as blood-cholesterol lowering agents, are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus.
2. Cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive drug, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.
3. Penicillin, the first antibiotic discovered, was isolated from the mould Penicillium notatum.
4. Streptokinase is produced by the bacterium Streptococcus.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(iv), and D-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q05 - Biocontrol agents and their target pests

questiontext.text:
Match the biological control agents with the target pests or organisms they control.

List I (Biocontrol Agent)List II (Target Pest / Organism)
A. Ladybird beetle(i) Butterfly caterpillars
B. Dragonflies(ii) Aphids
C. Bacillus thuringiensis(iii) Species-specific insects and arthropods
D. Nucleopolyhedrovirus(iv) Mosquitoes

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biocontrol relies on natural predation, microbial pathogens, and species-specific viruses to keep pest populations at manageable levels without toxic chemical pesticides.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. The Ladybird beetle (with red and black markings) is useful for getting rid of aphids.
2. Dragonflies are useful for getting rid of mosquitoes.
3. Bacillus thuringiensis spores are sprayed on brassicas and fruit trees to kill butterfly caterpillars when ingested.
4. Nucleopolyhedrovirus (a genus of baculoviruses) acts as a species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal agent attacking insects and other arthropods without harming non-target organisms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), and D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q06 - Biofertilisers and their roles in soil fertility

questiontext.text:
Match the biofertiliser organisms with their specific roles in enriching soil fertility.

List I (Biofertiliser)List II (Role)
A. Rhizobium(i) Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium in soil
B. Azotobacter(ii) Mycorrhizal fungus absorbing phosphorus from soil
C. Glomus(iii) Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium in paddy fields
D. Oscillatoria(iv) Symbiotic nitrogen fixation in leguminous root nodules

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biofertilisers include bacteria, fungi, and cyanobacteria that enrich soil nutrients through nitrogen fixation or enhanced mineral absorption.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Rhizobium forms symbiotic nodules on the roots of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms.
2. Azotobacter (along with Azospirillum) fixes atmospheric nitrogen while living freely in the soil.
3. Glomus forms mycorrhizal associations with plant roots, absorbing phosphorus from the soil and passing it to the plant.
4. Oscillatoria (along with Anabaena and Nostoc) is an autotrophic cyanobacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen and serves as an important biofertiliser in paddy fields.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(iv), B-(i), C-(ii), and D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q07 - Sewage treatment components and their descriptions

questiontext.text:
Match the terms associated with sewage treatment plants (STPs) with their correct descriptions.

List I (Term)List II (Description)
A. Primary sludge(i) Mesh-like masses of aerobic bacteria and fungal filaments
B. Flocs(ii) Anaerobic digestion of sludge producing inflammable biogas
C. Activated sludge(iii) Solids settled during physical filtration and sedimentation
D. Anaerobic sludge digesters(iv) Sedimented bacterial flocs formed after BOD reduction

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Municipal sewage treatment occurs in two sequential stages: primary physical treatment and secondary biological treatment using aerobic and anaerobic microbes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Primary sludge consists of all solids (such as grit, soil, and pebbles) that settle down during primary physical treatment by filtration and sedimentation.
2. Flocs are mesh-like structures formed by masses of aerobic bacteria associated with fungal filaments in aeration tanks.
3. Activated sludge is the sediment formed in the settling tank when bacterial flocs settle down after the BOD of the effluent is significantly reduced.
4. Anaerobic sludge digesters are large tanks where anaerobic bacteria digest the bacteria and fungi in the sludge, producing biogas (methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), and D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MATCH_Q08 - Scientists and institutions with contributions in microbial welfare

questiontext.text:
Match the scientists or institutions with their respective contributions to microbial applications in human welfare.

List I (Scientist / Institution)List II (Contribution)
A. Alexander Fleming(i) Developed biogas production technology in India
B. Ernest Chain and Howard Florey(ii) Chance discovery of penicillin from Penicillium notatum
C. IARI and KVIC(iii) Initiated Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan
D. Ministry of Environment and Forests(iv) Established full potential of penicillin as an effective antibiotic

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Key historical discoveries and institutional initiatives have translated microbial processes into large-scale medical, energy, and environmental solutions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Alexander Fleming made the chance discovery of penicillin while working on Staphylococci and observing inhibition around Penicillium notatum.
2. Ernest Chain and Howard Florey established the full potential of penicillin as an effective antibiotic, which was used extensively to treat wounded American soldiers in World War II.
3. IARI and KVIC (Indian Agricultural Research Institute and Khadi and Village Industries Commission) were mainly responsible for developing biogas production technology in India.
4. The Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to build sewage treatment plants and save major rivers from pollution.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), and D-(iii).

questiontext.text:
Match the fermented products or fuels with their characteristic production processes.

List I (Product / Fuel)List II (Production Process)
A. Toddy(i) Alcoholic beverages produced without distillation
B. Wine and beer(ii) Methane-rich gas produced by Methanobacterium on cellulosic waste
C. Whisky, brandy, and rum(iii) Traditional drink made by fermenting palm sap
D. Biogas(iv) Alcoholic beverages produced by distillation of fermented broth

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbial fermentation and anaerobic digestion yield distinct beverages and fuels depending on the substrate, microbe, and downstream processing.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pairing
1. Toddy is a traditional drink of southern India made by fermenting sap from palms.
2. Wine and beer are alcoholic beverages produced by yeast fermentation without distillation.
3. Whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.
4. Biogas is a predominantly methane-containing gas mixture produced when methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow anaerobically on cellulosic material.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), and D-(ii).
